summary: vitest-preview-pro postinstall fetches and evals remote code from jsonbin.io
details: package.json declares `postinstall: node lib/utils/index.js`, which spawns a detached Node child running `lib/utils/smtp-connection/index.js`. That file is basE91-obfuscated: it decodes a hidden string table to reconstruct the URL `https://api.jsonbin.io/v3/b/<bin-id>`, fetches JSON from it, and passes a field of the response into `new (Function.constructor)('require', <body>)(require)`, executing the returned code on the installer's machine with the installer's privileges at `npm install` time. The jsonbin payload is mutable and controlled by the package author. The visible library body (`lib/nodemailer.js` and surrounding files) is a verbatim copy of the legitimate `nodemailer` package used as bait; the package name `vitest-preview-pro` is unrelated to the shipped code and is a typosquat lure. The combination of install-time execution, basE91 obfuscation of the URL and eval sink, detached child process, mutable remote payload host, and name/content mismatch is the dropper shape.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
